{
  "research_question": "How does mouse navigation performance vary across five stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, and Sham) when assessed by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "descriptive_findings": [
    "Sham stimulation shows the poorest performance across all metrics: lowest Success rate (0.273), longest Time-to-Target (4.68s), lowest Path Efficiency (0.308), slowest Average Speed (10.74), and lowest AD (0.236)",
    "Combined stimulation yields the highest Success rate (0.780) and fastest Time-to-Target (2.56s), with high Path Efficiency (0.502) and Average Speed (12.83)",
    "Bright Visual Only performs comparably to Combined on Success (0.785 vs 0.780) and Time-to-Target (2.61s vs 2.56s), with slightly lower Path Efficiency and Speed",
    "ICMS Only and Dim Visual Only show intermediate performance, with Success rates of 0.685 and 0.673 respectively, and Time-to-Target around 3.05-3.14s",
    "AD values are highest for Combined (0.399) and Bright Visual Only (0.387), intermediate for ICMS Only (0.354), and lowest for Sham (0.236)",
    "Sample sizes vary substantially across paradigms: Combined dominates with 48,846 trials (63.6% of data), while Sham has only 3,505 trials (4.6%)"
  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "Success rate: Sham (0.273) vs Combined (0.780) shows a 2.85-fold difference, the largest absolute gap of 0.507",
    "Time-to-Target: Sham (4.68s) is 1.83× slower than Combined (2.56s), with an absolute difference of 2.12 seconds",
    "Path Efficiency: Sham (0.308) vs Combined (0.502) represents a 63% relative difference",
    "AD: Sham (0.236) vs Combined (0.399) shows a 69% relative increase, suggesting more variable heading directions in active stimulation conditions",
    "The Combined and Bright Visual Only paradigms cluster together with superior performance, while ICMS Only and Dim Visual Only form an intermediate tier, and Sham is distinctly inferior"
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "Active sensory stimulation—particularly combined ICMS and visual cues or bright visual cues alone—substantially improves mouse navigation performance compared to no stimulation. The Sham condition's poor performance establishes a clear baseline deficit, while the similarity between Combined and Bright Visual Only suggests that visual cues may be the primary driver of performance enhancement. The elevated angular dispersion (AD) in successful conditions likely reflects active exploration and course correction rather than disorientation, as it coincides with faster, more efficient paths. ICMS alone provides modest benefit over Sham but underperforms visual-based paradigms, suggesting limited efficacy as a standalone navigation aid in this task.",
  "limitations": [
    "Severe imbalance in sample sizes: Combined has 13.9× more trials than Sham, potentially affecting comparison reliability",
    "No statistical tests (ANOVA, post-hoc comparisons, confidence intervals) are provided to assess significance of group differences",
    "Mouse-level variation is not accounted for in these marginal means; some paradigms may have been tested with different mice or at different frequencies",
    "Temperature was fixed at 0.0, but this is an LLM generation parameter, not a biological experimental condition",
    "Path Efficiency shows extreme max value (29.8) suggesting possible outliers or calculation anomalies not addressed",
    "No information on trial-level dependencies, learning effects, or temporal dynamics within sessions"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct mixed-effects modeling with Mouse as a random effect to account for individual differences, followed by pairwise comparisons with appropriate multiple comparison correction. Examine interaction effects between stimulation type and task difficulty or trial number. Additionally, visualize distributions (boxplots, violin plots) to assess normality and identify outliers, particularly for Path Efficiency given its extreme maximum value."
}
